chapter_seo_title: Unlocking the Dark Secret of the Emperor's Power: "The Mandate of Heaven"
chapter_meta_description: Ji Lin learns the horrific truth behind the Mandate of Heaven: his family's throne was built on a pact of self-slaughter. A new law of the Dao-Twisted World is revealed.
og_title: The Bloody Price of the Crown
og_description: The truth is out. The Ji family's throne isn't a right—it's a curse of kin-slaughter. A lore-heavy chapter that rewrites the rules of power.
twitter_title: The Emperor's Secret is Out. It's Not Pretty.
twitter_description: Ji Lin learns the price of his throne is his own family's blood. The "Mandate of Heaven" in this world is far more terrifying than you'd think.

lore_anchors.definition: A divine right to rule in Chinese political thought. In the Dao-Twisted World, it is presented as a stolen fragment of ancient power that only a willing kinship-slaugtherer can bear.
A title for the Chinese emperor. Here, it is literalized: the imperial power takes the form of a dragon that physically marks its bearer.
A classic Chinese mythological motif. In this novel, it is used as a prison for the undead emperor.
A fictional sect fusing Zoroastrianism and Nestorian Christianity. They are the original owners of the Thousand Greats Record and view suffering as a path to power.
Ancient sorcerers or shamanic beings. According to the emperor, they once kept humans as livestock before the ancestors escaped to forge their own reality.
The imperial dynasty founded by the Ji family after the fall of the Great Qi.
An envoy from the Ao-Jing Sect. He has betrayed the new emperor by kidnapping Princess Anping.
The emperor's daughter who has been kidnapped.
